h1: Band saw blades for metal cutting — bimetal, carbide-tipped and CBN
intro: A band saw blade is the one consumable that decides what a band saw machine can do: the right cutting material, tooth form and tooth pitch cut faster, straighter and longer than the wrong one on any saw. NovoTech supplies WIKUS band saw blades — made in Germany by the world's largest band saw blade maker — welded to the length of your machine in Canada: M42 bimetal blades from the economical PRIMAR through the MARATHON, PROFLEX, SKALAR and SELEKTA GS, the coated PREMIUM versions and the X3000® blades for difficult alloys; carbide-tipped blades from the entry-level TAURUS and MARADUR to the FUTURA family for solid steel, the NE blades for aluminum and copper and the specialists for hardened parts; coated carbide blades for production; and CUBOGRIT® CBN blades that cut hardened HSS and tool steel above 55 HRC. Widths from 1/2″ to 4″ in every tooth pitch, for Bekamak, NovoTech value-line and any other horizontal or vertical band saw. Blade selection and pitch advice from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: Bimetal or carbide — which band saw blade do I need?
faq.a: A bimetal blade (M42 high-speed-steel teeth on a spring-steel back) is the right blade for a fabrication shop: structural profiles, tube, bundles and solid bar up to about 145,000 psi, mixed materials, on any band saw. A carbide-tipped blade cuts solid material two to three times faster and lasts longer, but it wants a rigid saw with enough motor power and band tension — the Bekamak production saws and most saws with a carbide package. The TAURUS and MARADUR are made to run on saws without a carbide package, so they are the first step up; stainless, titanium and nickel alloys call for the FUTURA VA and 718; aluminum and copper for the NE blades; hardened steel for the FUTURA SN or the CBN-coated CUBOGRIT.

faq.q: How do I choose the tooth pitch?
faq.a: By the contact length — the width of material the blade is in at any moment: 4 to 12 teeth should be in the cut. Thin-wall tube and small profiles need a fine pitch (10–14 TPI), bar of 2 to 4 inches a 3–4 or 2–3 TPI blade, and large solid material 1.4–2 TPI and coarser. A variable pitch (for example 3–4 TPI) runs quieter and resists vibration on profiles and bundles; a constant pitch is used on uniform solid material. Each blade's table on this page lists the pitches available in every width and the contact length each pitch is meant for.

faq.q: What do the product levels mean?
faq.a: WIKUS grades its blades: level 1 is the economical entry blade (PRIMAR, TAURUS, MARADUR), level 2 the universal production blade (MARATHON, PROFLEX, DUROSET, ECODUR), level 3 the high-performance blade for the highest cutting rates and blade life (SKALAR, SELEKTA GS, FUTURA) and level S the specialists for one job — hardened parts (FUTURA SN), large solid material (ARION FG), thin-walled tube (TCT).

faq.q: Which blade width and length fits my saw?
faq.a: The width and thickness are set by the saw's wheels and guides — 1″ × 0.035″ on most 10″ to 13″ shop saws, 1-1/4″ × 0.042″ and 1-1/2″ × 0.050″ on the mid-size automatic saws, 2″ to 3-1/8″ on the double-column production saws. The length is the loop length of your machine; we weld the blade to it from coil. Send the saw make and model and we look it up.

faq.q: Can carbide blades run on my saw?
faq.a: On the Bekamak BMSO and BMSY automatic saws, the double-column saws and any saw with a carbide package (high band tension, rigid guides, enough motor power) — yes, any of the carbide blades on this page. On a lighter saw, use the TAURUS or MARADUR, which are set and ground to run without the carbide package, or stay with a level 3 bimetal blade such as the SKALAR M42.

faq.q: What is the X3000® cutting material?
faq.a: A WIKUS high-speed steel with higher hardness and toughness than M42, used on the MARATHON, SKALAR and SELEKTA GS X3000 blades for difficult-to-machine materials and special alloys — stainless, nickel and titanium alloys, high-strength steels — where an M42 edge dulls early but a carbide blade is not justified.

faq.q: Do you stock blades and weld them in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — the common widths are stocked as coil in Mississauga and welded and annealed to your length; the complete WIKUS program is available to order. Tell us the saw, the materials you cut and the sizes, and we propose the blade and the pitch — and we are happy to run a test blade on a difficult job.

origin_feature.title: Made in Germany by WIKUS
origin_feature.text: WIKUS has made band saw blades in Spangenberg, Germany since 1958 — bimetal, carbide-tipped and coated blades for metal cutting, developed in its own Technical Competence Center and cut and welded to length by its partners worldwide.
